title: Construct Binary Search Tree from Preorder Traversal
statement: `preorder` holds the values of a binary search tree listed in preorder: a node's value first, then everything in its left subtree, then everything in its right subtree. In this BST, every value inside a node's left subtree is strictly smaller than that node's value, and every value inside its right subtree is strictly larger. Rebuild the tree that yields this sequence and return its root. The input is guaranteed to come from some BST.
constraints: All values in preorder are distinct.
notes:
## Intuition

Inserting the values one by one into an empty BST rebuilds the right tree, but each insertion walks from the root, so that is O(n²) on a chain. The BST property gives a faster way: in preorder, a node is followed first by its left subtree, whose values are all smaller than the node, and then by its right subtree. So while reading the array left to right, every subtree is the longest run of upcoming values that stays below an upper bound inherited from its ancestors.

## Approach

1. Keep `index`, the next value of `preorder` to place.
2. `build(upper)` builds the subtree whose values must stay below `upper`. If the array is used up or the next value is larger than `upper`, that value belongs higher up, so return `null`.
3. Otherwise make a `node` from the next value and advance `index`.
4. Its left subtree takes the following values that are smaller than `node.val`: `build(node.val)`.
5. Its right subtree takes the values after that which still fit under the parent's bound: `build(upper)`.
6. Start with `build(Infinity)`, since the root has no bound.

## Example 1, step by step

`preorder = [8,5,1,7,10,12]`.

- `build(∞)` makes 8. Its left is `build(8)`, which makes 5.
- 5's left is `build(5)`, which makes 1. 1's children see 7, which is above 1 and above 5, so both are `null`.
- 5's right is `build(8)`: 7 fits, so 7 becomes 5's right child. 7's children see 10, which is above 7 and 8: `null`.
- 8's right is `build(∞)`: 10 fits. 10's left sees 12 > 10, `null`; 10's right is `build(∞)`, which makes 12.

The tree in level order is `[8,5,10,1,7,null,12]`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): each value is turned into a node once, and each `build` call either places a value or returns at once.
- Space: O(h) for the recursion, up to O(n) when the tree is a chain.

## Pitfalls

- The right subtree must use the parent's bound `upper`, not `Infinity`, or values from an ancestor's right side get pulled in too early.
- Check `index === preorder.length` before reading `preorder[index]`.
- `index` is shared by all calls; passing it by value would place values twice.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `index` | position of the next value in `preorder` to place |
| `upper` | every value in the subtree being built must stay below this |
| `node` | the node just created from `preorder[index]` |

narration.2: index points at the next preorder value still waiting to be placed.
narration.4: build creates the subtree whose values must all stay below upper.
narration.5: No values left, or the next value is too big to belong in this subtree?
narration.6: Then this subtree is empty; the value belongs to an ancestor's right side.
narration.8: In preorder the subtree's root comes first, so the next value becomes this node.
narration.9: That value is now placed; move on to the next one.
narration.10: The left subtree takes the following values smaller than this node.
narration.11: The right subtree takes what remains below the inherited bound.
narration.12: Hand the finished subtree back to its parent.
narration.15: The root has no upper bound, so start with Infinity.
